lesson_title: The Long Way to Your Tap
hook_text: When you open a tap, the water may have travelled more than twenty kilometres through pipes and been cleaned in five steps to reach you.
clip_script: Midmar Dam, near Howick in KwaZulu-Natal. Brown water flows from the dam into a treatment works. Screens catch sticks and leaves. Chemicals make the dirt clump together and sink. Sand filters catch the tiny bits. A little chlorine kills the germs. Now the water is clean and clear. Huge pumps push it through pipes to a reservoir on a hill, and from there it flows down, under the streets, all the way to a tap in a school. Turn it on, and there it is.
visual_style: Whiteboard flow line from left to right: a dam, a screen, a tank with clumps sinking, a sand filter, a chlorine drop, a reservoir on a hill, and pipes to a house tap, each step numbered.
mood: Clever and satisfying, like seeing how a machine works inside.
pacing: One step per beat along the flow line, then a quick replay from dam to tap.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and follow the pipe from your tap as far as you can see it.
